newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel continued to decline against the dollar on Tuesday in dull trading as investors remained on the sidelines, dealers said.
"Activity continues to be very low and investors are sitting on the fence waiting to see where the shekel is going," said Ilan Zadka at United Mizrahi Bank.
"The recent decline of the shekel is meaningless since the volume is low and one deal can move the market," he said.

The shekel has lost 1.85 percent since last Wednesday but Zadka said he believes that in the near term the shekel will start rising against the dollar. "There is no reason for the shekel's decline. Its only a question of time before it starts rising again," he said.
Zadka added that spreads are still high at 100 points. "The market is very nervous and the banks are taking no risk," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5730 shekels against 3.5690 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8794 against 3.8786 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.1704 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.1761 on Monday, and against the mark at 2.0347 shekels compared with 2.0440 on Monday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5700 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
